findings.description: Port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing anyone on the internet to attempt SSH login/brute-force against the portal server.
The egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting data exfiltration or C2 communication from a compromised instance.

AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in the EC2 user_data script, which is readable in plaintext by anyone with instance metadata access (e.g., via SSRF) or describe-instance-attribute permissions.
The instance does not specify root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root volume data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required", leaving IMDSv1 enabled and instance credentials/metadata exposed to SSRF attacks.
The instance is launched in a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch and an internet gateway default route, directly exposing it (including open SSH) to the internet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so data on the attached disk is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot derives from an unencrypted EBS volume, so the backup copy of the data is also unencrypted at rest.
The VPC flow log S3 bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving sensitive network telemetry unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or ACL/policy controls are defined for the flow log bucket, risking accidental public exposure of network logs.
Versioning is not enabled on the log bucket, so log objects can be overwritten or deleted without recovery, undermining audit integrity.
force_destroy = true allows the audit log bucket and all flow log objects to be deleted in a single terraform destroy, destroying forensic evidence.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, automatically exposing workloads to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, automatically exposing workloads to the internet.
The VPC's default security group is not restricted via aws_default_security_group, so resources attached to it may inherit permissive allow-all intra-group rules.
